newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe says won't renew all white farmers' leases.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe says won't renew all white farmers' leases.

text.p: Zimbabwe's government, under fire for slow progress on resettling landless blacks, said on Sunday it would not renew all state farm leases held by whites.

"Once the leases expire we will give them to our hungry people, some of whom are virtually squatters in their own land," Land and Water Resources Minister Kumbirai Kangai told a ruling Zanu-PF party conference in the second city of Bulawayo.
He gave no indication of the numbers involved. Zimbabwe has some 4,000 white commercial farmers, most of whom own their farms.

Kangai's ministry was involved in a scandal last year after top officials allocated themselves farms earmarked for resettlement. The minister told the conference his officials had now set up procedures to ensure transparency in farm allocation.
Only about 60,000 families have been resettled since independence in 1980, compared with an original target of 160,000 within three years.
